title: fix(ui): isolate live theme state between parallel unit tests
body:
## What changed

Unit tests keep live theme tokens on their own thread.
Each test thread starts with the dark theme.
The application keeps its existing process-wide lock and poison recovery.
The storage helper moves to `theme/live.rs`.

## Cause

Parallel tests changed the process-wide theme while other tests scanned overlay colors.
Color-vision selection belongs to each world, but its palette also reads the live theme ground.

`a_fresh_test_thread_starts_with_the_default_dark_theme` checks the default after another thread selects Light.

Restoring upstream's original storage made both pins fail again.
Restoring the fix made both pass again.

Three full parallel `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` runs passed.
Each run reported 1055 passed, zero failed, and six existing ignored tests.

None.

title: fix(ui): show tilted heights along the tool axis
body:
Stacked on #2418 (merge #2418 first)

## What changed

Tilted height planes now use the operation frame and the shared `fold_height` resolver.
The rectangle spans the stock in local XY.
Its corners and label anchors pass through `TiltedFrame::to_world`.
Height echoes and viewport labels state the local distance along the tool axis.
Draft tilt edits update these values before Apply.
Invalid tilts hide the planes and show the existing named refusal.
`operation::region_z` uses the same folded height.
Untilted planes and text retain their existing behavior.

The original stack used parent head `3e62cea0a`.
This branch also includes the requested pocket island and depth validation fixes from parent head `302b097254569c239d5d5e3f28ff06625080b92c`.
The display changes address #2416.
The decision record is `docs/decisions/2416-tilted-height-display.md`.

## Cause

The display resolved heights as setup Z and drew horizontal stock-XY rectangles.
It did not read the tilted tool axis.
On the asymmetric test stock, the correct clearance is 21 along the axis.
The old display placed a clearance corner at local height -5.
The old region read returned 10 instead of the fold coordinate 14.

## Tests

Seven pins in `egui_app::heights_tests` failed before this fix:

- `tilted_height_planes_use_tool_axis_and_local_stock_corners`
- `tilted_height_echoes_use_tool_axis_on_asymmetric_stock`
- `invalid_draft_tilt_hides_height_planes_and_names_the_missing_direction`

- `tilted_height_labels_show_local_axis_distance`

Ten mutation checks failed, then passed after restoration:

- Restore the old region-height resolver.
- Restore the old plane rendering code.
- Restore the old height echo and its page context.
- Replace local stock bounds with world bounds.
- Remove the origin-Z shift from plane placement.

- Restore the old viewport label value.

The old region mutation retained the parent resolver adapter so the stack could compile.
The mutated region function matched upstream/main.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 253 steps, zero failures.
Clippy then requested an equivalent closure simplification.
All 12 height tests passed again after that change.

- #2134: `heights.rs` changes `missing_source`. This PR changes `region_z`.
- #2253: `operations.rs` changes `strategy_names`. This PR changes `height_echo`.
- #2149: `operations.rs` changes warning formatting. It also adds separate module declarations in `lib.rs`.
- #2185 and #1330: `lib.rs` adds separate module declarations. This PR registers `height_display`.

title: fix(motion): keep a multi-piece pocket's eroded area when no sliver drops
body:
## What changed

The post-merge batch gate on main `3e47b898b` failed on
`adaptive_entry_pieces::a_narrow_second_piece_names_its_ramp_stand_in_at_each_level`.

**Cause:** #2383 (for #2232) added `machining2d::pocket::non_sliver_center`.
It sent every multi-piece cutter-center area (two or more outer loops)
through a `Region::from_slices` rebuild, even when the sliver scan dropped
nothing. Clipper's normalisation restarts each loop at another vertex, so a
multi-piece pocket's pass starts moved. The narrow second piece's 1x1
center square started at (56, 6) instead of (56, 5), and the test's named
site no longer matched. The entry was still a named ramp (no gouge, no
unnamed plunge), but the move was an unintended side effect and not part of
#2232's decision.

**Fix:** `non_sliver_center` returns the plain `region.offset(-erode)`
unchanged unless at least one sliver is actually removed. Regions without
slivers now come out exactly as they did before #2383, and #2232's sliver
drop still applies where a sliver exists. Not a revert: #2383's stock-reach
clearing and sliver filter stay. The reasoning is in
`docs/decisions/2426-adaptive-entry-red.md`.

## Evidence

- Before the fix, on `3e47b898b`, the test fails with: `no named ramp stand-in for the pass start (56.000, 5.000) at Z -4.000 ... notes: ["entry: the pass start (56.000, 6.000) at Z -4.000 ... ramp along the pass instead", ...]`
- After the fix, all 5 tests of `adaptive_entry_pieces` pass.
- New pin `machining2d::pocket::non_sliver_tests::a_multi_piece_center_without_slivers_is_the_plain_offset` (motion lib) fails when the fix is disabled and passes with it.

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `e10ba5ba3`: 20 steps, 0 failed (motion lib incl. adaptive_troch tests that share `non_sliver_center`; motion adaptive_hsm, climb_direction, corner_arc_radius, corner_blend, entry_arc, optimal_load, predrilled_entry, refusal_ghost, rest_zigzag, rest2d, shape_masks, solid_law, top_z_level, xy_arc_entry; app pick_agnostic, pocket_overhead, solid_law_goldens).
- `adaptive_entry_pieces` (motion): 5/5 pass, including the failing test.
- `shoulder_adaptive` (app, #2383's own suite, pins the sliver drop and the outside-stock clearing): 9/9 pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

The release heavy lanes and the batch tier. The next post-merge run is the confirmation that #2426 asks for.

Changelog: Multi-piece pockets keep their pass starts again; the sliver filter from #2383 no longer reorders pocket areas that have no sliver (#2426)
Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #2426

title: fix(app): every operation's approach starts over the setup's WCS origin
body:
## What changed

Most mill generators seed their path at X0 Y0 on the clearance plane. That point is the world origin. The opening rapid started there, so these items read the world origin and not G54:
- the viewport (the drawn approach);
- the simulation link between operations;
- the CL `START` line;
- the post engine's `StartX/Y/Z`.

The posted move blocks were already correct, because a post writes only the end of each move.

The fix:
- New `Toolpath::seat_approach` (`crates/cl/src/cl/path_approach.rs`). When the first move is a rapid that leaves the seed, the start of that rapid moves to the WCS origin (X/Y) on the same plane. The end of the rapid does not change.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` calls it after generation. The call comes before the yaw exit, the fixture routing and the verify laws, so those laws judge the new rapid. The origin comes from `wcs_context`, which is the same origin that the post subtracts. A 3+2 path reads the origin in its local frame (`TiltedFrame::to_local`).
- These paths do not change: paths that open at their own first point (holes, plasma, sinker, lathe, wire, rotary, 3D roughing, adaptive trochoidal), and a zero-length seed rapid.

The cause has existed since 942a36d65 (#690 / #697, v0.17). It is not a 0.23 regression. The reproduction and the family list are on #2382.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2382-wcs-start.md`.

## Readings

- Reporter's project (local copy, not attached): each operation opened with a rapid from X0 Y0 at the clearance height. G54 is at a stock corner far from that point. The project does not post, because of a correct refusal that is not related to this issue (Home after Pause).
- Fixture (G54 at X40 Y20 Z10.5): on main, the face and the parallel finish start at (0, 0, 30). With the fix, they start at (40, 20, 30).

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/wcs_start.rs`:
  - `a_2d_operation_starts_over_the_wcs_origin` (fails on main)
  - `a_3d_operation_starts_over_the_wcs_origin` (fails on main)
  - `a_hole_operation_starts_over_its_first_hole`
  - `the_posted_program_measures_from_g54_and_never_visits_the_world_origin`
- `crates/cl/tests/origin_approach.rs`:
  - `seat_approach_moves_the_seeded_start_to_the_wcs_origin`
  - `seat_approach_leaves_other_openings_alone`

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`. A change in `cl` makes the quick gate fall back to batch. I ran the steps of the crates downstream of `cl` (`--only debug cl post sim motion app ui clippy`): 804 steps, 0 failed, about 116 min. I did not run the geometry, kernel and tools steps, because those crates do not depend on `cl`.
- No golden and no count changed. `golden_cl`, `first_router_part`, `axis_direction` and `wcs_rotation_control` pass without edits.

## Not exercised

- The GUI was not started. The viewport reading comes from the toolpath data that the viewport draws.
- A 3+2 path with a moved WCS has no own pinning test. The code reads the origin through `to_local`, and the existing tilt suites pass.
- 5-axis contour and parallel (stamped finishing paths) have no own pinning test with a moved WCS.
- A separate display question is still open: the chain pick ring and the toolpath in an aligned setup. This PR does not change it.

Changelog: The opening approach of each milling operation now starts over the setup's WCS origin, not the world origin. This applies to the viewport, the simulation and the program start point.

Effort: high

Fixes #2382

title: fix(operation): read a tilted op's reference heights along its tool axis
body:
## What changed

A tilted (3+1 / 3+2, `tilt.a_deg`/`b_deg`) operation took its reference heights - Top/Bottom of stock, Top/Bottom of model, Work offset - as the setup's world Z and only subtracted the plane origin's Z. It never measured along the turned tool axis. On #2389's bar (10 Y x 30 Z, centred on A) a Slot at A 90 with Top = Top of stock got 15 along the axis instead of 5, so it cut air. On other sides of an asymmetric stock it would plunge to the wrong depth.

- New `camcraft_app::operation::fold_height` (`crates/app/src/operation/tilt_heights.rs`). Under a non-upright tilt, each reference height is the referenced geometry's extent along the tool axis (`TiltedFrame::z_local` over its facets). It is returned as `z_local + origin.z`, so the existing `- origin.z` fold in `run_job` / `source_region` gives exactly the local value.
- Where it is used: the generation heights (`collect_job` through `resolve_params_folded`), the Contour/Pocket/Trace section plane (`section_z_of`) and the area-controls cut plane (`boundary_ctx`).
- Unchanged: Fixed heights keep the shipped `h - origin.z` law (pinned by `tilt.rs`). A Selection reference keeps the setup resolve, because a tilted op refuses a picked source first. Untilted ops and upright tilts (A0 B0) read the setup resolve verbatim, so prismatic paths and goldens keep their bits.
- `resolve_params` now delegates to `resolve_params_with` (the resolver is passed in). The refusal wording is unchanged.
- The viewport planes and the Heights tab's "(= Z ...)" echo are display-only and were split out to #2416 (P3, filed). Decision record: `docs/decisions/2389-tilt-heights-axis.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, in the new file `crates/app/tests/tilt_heights.rs`:
- `a_slot_at_a90_reads_top_of_stock_along_the_tool_axis`: the issue's proof. Clearance along the axis is 15 (main gives 25) and the bottom is 4.
- `an_offset_bar_reads_its_own_side_at_a_minus_90_and_the_underside`: an asymmetric stock (Y -1..11, Z -20..10) with a plane origin off the world origin.
  - A -90, origin (2,0,3): top 11; clearance 21 along the axis (main gives 17).
  - A0 B180, origin Z 3: top 23. This case also exercises the `+ origin.z` hand-off.
- `a_tilted_contour_sections_the_model_along_the_tool_axis`: a tilted Contour on a part, with Top/Bottom of model. On main it is refused with "no material at z = 14.000"; with the fix it contours at local 4..3.

Mutation check (revert, then restore):
- `collect_job` set back to the setup resolve: tests 1 and 2 go red (25 vs 15; 17 vs 21).
- `section_z_of` given no frame: test 3 goes red.

title: feat(post): wrapped A on the Tormach microARC 4 (G93, cumulative A)
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach.cps` no longer refuses an A that changes inside an operation on an A-about-X machine. It now posts it as wrapped (simultaneous) A, based on mkinney's four PathPilot Hub readings on #796 (v2.14.4, 770MX SIM, 4th axis on):

- **A is cumulative.** PathPilot treats A as plain degrees with no rollover (A350 -> `G1 A10` turned back 340 deg). Each target is the nearest equivalent of the held angle: 179 -> 181, 359 -> 361, never back through 0. A count past the stated travel is refused by name.
- **A turning X Y Z feed is G93.** `F = 1 / t`, where t (min) = max((the tip's path relative to the part + one rounding step) / the programmed feed, the posted |dA| / the stated A rate). F is floored to 0.001, so rounding only ever slows a move. Neither the cutting feed nor the A rate is exceeded. The rate comes from `rotaryRate` (#885).
- **An A-only feed stays G94**, with F in deg/min under the same time law (Hub reading 4). Feeds that don't turn A are unchanged. G94 is restated before any motion that is not a G93 feed and at every section end.
- **Turning moves are split onto their segment.** The machine moves XYZ in a line while A turns, so the tip relative to the part bows off the stream's segment. Each turning move (rapids too) is split into 2^k pieces until the bow is within 0.005 mm (at most 256 pieces, else refused by name).
- **A is reset between operations:** as before (#785), each section restates its first A as -180..180 after `G53 G0 Z0`, so a wrap that ended at A300 unwinds at the top of Z.
- **Refused by name:** a machine file with no A rate ("states no A feed rate"), a count past the travel ("A counts on through 360 (PathPilot does not roll A over)"), an arc / canned cycle / probe move that would turn A, a turning move from an unknown start, and a move that still bows after 256 splits.
- `assets/machines/tormach-770mx-microarc4.mch` now states A `max_normal_speed` 360 deg/min. That is the rate the Hub ran as asked. It is conservative: no Tormach rate could be cited with confidence.
- Docs: the tester-kit README, `first-4axis-part.md` and `continuous-4-axis.md` (with its site test), plus `docs/decisions/796-tormach-wrapped-a.md`. The kit's `.camproj` was re-saved by its own test, so it carries the A rate.

Fork branch based on upstream `main` at 4e8616b (not a cut tag), so the #885 rule and the current post are in.

## How tested

New pins in `crates/app/tests/tormach_wrapped_a.rs` (10 tests):
- `a_long_xyz_move_takes_its_time_from_the_feed`: `G93 G1 X50 Y0 Z0 A1 F11.999` (50 mm at F600)
- `a_mostly_rotary_move_takes_its_time_from_the_a_rate`: `G1 X51 Y0 Z0 A91 F4` (90 deg at 360 deg/min)
- `g94_comes_back_before_an_xyz_only_feed_and_a_turns_in_deg_per_min`
- `a_counts_on_through_180_and_360_never_back_through_0`
- `the_next_operation_resets_a_at_the_safe_z`
- `a_section_that_ends_in_g93_restates_g94_before_m5`
- `a_turning_move_off_the_axis_is_split_onto_its_chord`: every posted point, turned back into the part, lies on the stream's chord, and each piece is held to both rates
- `a_count_past_the_travel_is_refused_by_name`, `a_machine_with_no_a_rate_is_refused_by_name`, `the_microarc_states_its_a_rate`

Golden: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc` is the microARC kit's job plus a real Rotary Parallel (1/8" ball) on the bar. It is pinned by `microarc_test_part::a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_posts_wrapped_a`, which replaces `a_wrapped_op_on_the_test_part_is_refused_by_name` and also checks A unwrapping, G93 on every turning XYZ feed, G94 elsewhere, and G94 at the section end.

Updated: `tormach_fourth_axis::an_a_that_changes_inside_an_operation_posts_wrapped_a` (was `..._is_refused`). In `fourth_axis_pose`, the two fanuc tests on the microARC file now place A with a rapid first, because that file now states an A rate and the #885 rule asks for it. The recorded `rotary.refusal` golden for tormach (tilt-head machine) now names the B tilt refusal instead.

Gate (macOS, debug, targeted - `cargo xtask gate quick` plans every app suite because a new golden is shared test input, so the touched suites ran instead): every camcraft-app test binary that names Tormach / the microARC (69 binaries, incl. `tormach_wrapped_a`, `microarc_test_part`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `first_4axis_part`, `index_swing`, `tormach_post`, `rotary_feed_cap`, `recorded_post_streams`) and every camcraft-post binary that names Tormach or the recorded streams (45 binaries, incl. `script_tormach`, `explain_tormach`, `recorded_streams`): all green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app` on the four changed test files `-D warnings`: clean. `site/tests/test_first_4axis_part.py`: the updated tests pass; `test_machine_and_post_are_the_shipped_ones` fails the same way on upstream main (machine name not in `posting.rs`), not touched here.

## Not exercised

- No real cut, and this exact program has not been run in the Hub. The readings cover single test moves only.
- PathPilot's A soft limits. The file keeps -360..360, and a wrap past it is refused.

## Hub check (before trusting it on the 770MX + microARC 4)

Run slowly (feed override 25-50 %, single block for the first lines), with the tool lifted 1" above the work offset (air cut):
1. Post the golden's WRAP op (or `wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`) and load it in the Hub 770MX SIM with the 4th axis on. Confirm it loads with no error on `G93` / `G94` lines and no "F word missing".
2. Watch the A DRO on a stretch that passes 180 (e.g. line 1393 of the golden, A180 -> A185.757): A must keep counting up, never swing back through 0.
3. Time one long G93 line against its F (time = 1/F min). Check one A-only `G1 A.. F360` runs at 6 deg/s.
4. Confirm the control is back in G94 after the WRAP op (Status tab / the next op's feeds run at their ipm).
5. Check PathPilot's A soft limits (jog A past +360 / -360 in the SIM) and report them on #796, so the machine file's travel can be stated.
6. Only then air-cut on the real machine at a low override, the bar in the chuck, a hand on feed hold.

Changelog: Tormach PathPilot post: continuous (wrapped) A on the microARC 4 - A counts on past 360, turning feeds in G93 held to the feed and the stated A rate (360 deg/min); refused by name when the machine states no A rate or the count passes the A travel (#796)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #796

title: fix(sim): play the stock up to the first operation with no toolpath
body:
Stacked on #2192 (base `issue/2181-sim-precalc`). Retarget this PR to `main` before #2192 merges.

## What changed

- The stock playback (the transport's traced stock) plays the program in posting order up to the first operation that has no toolpath. It stops there. It does not skip that operation to cut the operations after it.
  - `posting::program_ops_until_ungenerated` and `stock_sim::plan_program_until_ungenerated` are new. Only `PlaySeed::gather` uses them.
  - `posting::program_ops` and `stock_sim::plan_program` keep their behaviour. The post and the Deviate verdict still refuse the program by name ("<op>: no toolpath yet - generate it first").
  - `PlayIndex::stop()` names the operation. `PlayIndex::position_at` holds the stock at the end of the plan when the playhead is on an operation at or after the stop.
  - When the first operation has no toolpath, the playback shows the uncut stock of that operation's setup.
- A separate line under the transport bar names the stop: "Stock simulation stops before 2D Contour1: it has no toolpath. Generate it to see the rest." (`play_precalc::stop_readout`, `play_precalc::transport_row`). The stop is not added to the status line. Thus the generation notes of a clean operation do not get the "!" error mark.
- The remaining playback refusal reads "simulation shows the uncut stock: <why>". It replaces "traced playback refused: <why> - the sheet stands".

title: fix(ui): cache pick highlight geometry and batch stroke draws
body:
## What changed

- Added thread-local weak lookup indexes (`resolve_chain_arc`, `patches_arc`, `patch_rings_arc`) in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature/index.rs`.
- Removed per-triangle heap allocations in `digest_of` and hoisted lattice construction in `patches` and `patch_rings` inside `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs`.
- Added `SHARED_FEATURES_CACHE` (`Weak<[Triangle]>`, cap 32) in `crates/app/src/model/geometry.rs` so repeated `features_of` reads skip `digest_of`.
- Added non-cloning `toolpath_nonempty` and `toolpath_warning_count` in `crates/app/src/model.rs`, used them in `operation::stamp::status_of` and `browser_tree::op_row`, and added `History::revision_token` in `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs`.
- Switched `Arc<Features>` lookups in `crates/app/src/operation/{selection.rs, stitch.rs}`, `crates/app/src/pick/{face.rs, feature_sel.rs}`, and `crates/ui/src/{edge_pick.rs, interact.rs, state.rs}` to `*_arc` helpers.
- Added `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight.rs` (`HighlightCache`) to resolve selected, hovered, and row-hovered outlines once per state change.
- Added `crates/ui/src/pick_highlight_mesh.rs` to tessellate each highlight layer into one cached `egui::Shape::Mesh` in `pick_ink::paint` and `shell::viewport_panel`.
- Added `crates/ui/src/frame_cache.rs` and `crates/ui/src/panel_cache.rs` on `State` to cache world vertices, cutting regions and outlines, toolpath overlay lines, non-transient `world::Scene` plus digest, Geometry chips, 3-2-1 datum checks, selection account, unresolved notes, operation status banners, and browser operation rows.
- Review fix (`b654e0502`): `WorldVertsEntry` in `crates/ui/src/frame_cache.rs` keeps a `Weak<[Triangle]>` of the source facets, not a raw address. A released source cannot match, and its address cannot be reused while the entry holds the `Weak`. Dead entries are pruned on each lookup.
- Added architecture decision record in `docs/decisions/2201-highlighter-frame-perf.md`.

## Cause

- On models with many chains or facets, `features_of` re-hashed triangle buffers and `resolve_chain` re-walked and split chains repeatedly during frame, highlight, and panel queries.
- `pick_ink::paint` and `shell::viewport_panel` emitted two individual `Shape::LineSegment` shapes per projected segment per frame.
- `world::collect`, `toolpath_lines`, `stamp::status_of`, `browser_tree::op_row`, `op_page`, and `geo_page` rebuilt and cloned vertices, outlines, warnings, and toolpaths on every frame even when inputs stayed unchanged.

The review fix replaces blocking `ureq` with `reqwest` and a current-thread `tokio` runtime so cancellation interrupts active requests. ## What changed

- **`camcraft_app::ai`** (new, `crates/app/src/ai/`):
  - `endpoint` - URL parse (WHATWG `url`; user info, query and fragment refused), loopback test (`localhost`, 127/8, `::1`, IPv4-mapped), `admit` (offline-only reaches loopback alone; plain `http://` off the machine is refused, key or not), `admit_addrs` (the resolver's half).
  - `presets` - Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses (GPT and Codex), Gemini `generateContent` (all `https://`); Ollama `http://localhost:11434/v1`, Unsloth Studio `http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`, LM Studio `http://localhost:1234/v1`, llama.cpp `llama-server` `http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1` (`--jinja` named in the label).
  - `wire` - the request path and body per provider. Tool-call envelopes are echoed in each provider's own shape (Anthropic content blocks, Chat `tool_calls` message, Responses `output` items incl. reasoning, Gemini content incl. `thoughtSignature`); consecutive tool results merge into one Anthropic user message / one Gemini turn. Model ids are checked so they cannot add a query or climb the Gemini path. Fallback (prompt-JSON / Q&A) payloads go into the system prompt with no tools.
  - `probe` - Ollama `/api/show` capabilities -> tools / vision / fallback mode.
  - `secret` - `ApiKey` has no `Display` and a redacted `Debug`, refuses control characters (no header injection); lookup is the env var (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`) first, then the keychain.
  - `http` (native only) - the client. `admit` runs before anything resolves; the agent's resolver refuses non-loopback addresses when offline-only or plain http; **no redirects followed**, **no proxy from the environment**, connect/total timeouts, auth only in headers (`x-api-key`, `Authorization: Bearer`, `x-goog-api-key`), errors carry the host, status and the provider's message - never the key.
  - `keychain` (native only) - `load` / `store` / `forget` under the service `camcraft-ai`.
- **`prefs.json`** gains `aiOfflineOnly` (written only when on); `ViewPrefs` has no field that could hold a key.
- **AI Chat dock** (`crates/ui`): native builds use the new `transport_http::HttpTransport` (presets map to the endpoints above; the key comes from env/keychain or the step is refused by name; an Ollama model without the `tools` capability is refused by name in the native-tools preset, pointing at the Prompt-JSON / Q&A presets). The "Offline only" switch is restored from and saved to `prefs.json`. The browser build keeps the offline-only `DefaultTransport` (now `cfg(wasm32)`).

- New `crates/app/tests/ai_http.rs` against a fake loopback HTTP server (no real key: a fixed placeholder sent only to 127.0.0.1): `anthropic_messages_wire_format`, `openai_chat_completions_wire_format`, `openai_responses_wire_format`, `gemini_generate_content_wire_format`, `local_runtimes_send_no_auth_header`, `ollama_capability_probe`, `offline_only_blocks_every_non_loopback_host_before_a_socket` (every cloud preset plus TEST-NET / private / IPv6 hosts refused in < 500 ms, plus the resolver check), `plain_http_off_this_machine_is_refused`, `redirects_are_not_followed_and_errors_never_carry_the_key`. 9/9 pass.
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs::offline_only_survives_and_the_file_stores_zero_keys` (the file's keys are exactly the known five; no "key"/"token"/"secret"/"password"/"bearer").
- Unit tests in `ai::endpoint`, `ai::presets`, `ai::secret`, `ai::wire`, `ai::probe`, and `transport_http::every_panel_preset_has_an_endpoint`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (fell back to batch: Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock changed): geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app (incl. `ai_http`, `view_prefs`) and ui suites all **ok** (35.5 min). Clippy `-D warnings` FAILS only on `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs:115` `MIN_LABEL_PX` never used - pre-existing on upstream main since PR #2095, tracked in #2104 / PR #2111; no other lint in the touched crates.

- No call to a real provider or a real local runtime (no key in tests, no network in tests).
- The OS keychain itself (`keychain::load/store/forget`) is not called by any test - a test would prompt or write the developer's real keychain; the lookup order is pinned with an injected keychain.
- No UI for entering/storing a key yet: keys come from the env vars, or from the keychain if stored by other means (service `camcraft-ai`, account `anthropic`/`openai`/`gemini`). A key-entry field is a follow-up.
- Streaming responses (each step is one complete response, as the dock's worker expects).

title: refactor(log): library and UI diagnostics become tracing events
body:
## What changed

The last slice of #163, after PR #222 (app seams: save/open/post/generate/commands) and PR #969 (app library eprintln!s and the budget-refusal events). With this, no diagnostic in the library or UI crates bypasses the one `tracing` subscriber any more.

- **Library crates** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): every non-test `eprintln!` is now a `tracing` event - refusals and fallbacks at `warn` (refused move/builder axis or C angle; multi-axis moves held vertical or radial, a rotary start on the axis, a degenerate drive curve skipped; a non-finite sim path left out or move held still; the dual iso-surface falling back to marching tetrahedra; a missing starter tool catalog), the opt-in `CAMCRAFT_PROFILE_PROJECTION` profile lines at `info`. The text of each line is unchanged.
- **Standalone bins** (`camcraft-cl`, `-geometry`, `-motion`, `-sim`, `-tools`): each installs a stderr subscriber with the app's filter rule (`CAMCRAFT_LOG`, else `RUST_LOG`, else `info`), so the converted library warnings still reach their terminal. Their own `println!` reports and usage errors are the CLI's answer and stay as they are.
- **UI**: the `diag` seam (#31) now emits `tracing` events natively (target `camcraft_ui`, `warn`/`info`) instead of `eprintln!`/`println!`; wasm32 still goes to the browser console. The native window (`shell_window.rs`, `shell_window/frame.rs`), GPU bring-up (`gpu_init.rs`), Cmd+Q hook (`os_quit.rs`) and the headless proof (`shell.rs`) now speak through the seam, so the law test's allow-list shrinks to the seam and test-only code (`gpu.rs`'s test module, `headless_gpu.rs`'s `device_for_test`, whose "SKIPPED - NOT a pass" line must show in a test run with no subscriber).

**Dependencies.** No new crate: `tracing` and `tracing-subscriber` are already workspace dependencies (root `Cargo.toml`, since PR #222) and in `Cargo.lock`; this PR adds `{ workspace = true }` lines for them to the five library crates and `tracing` (plus `tracing-subscriber` as a dev-dependency) to `camcraft-ui`. `Cargo.lock` gains only those dependency edges. No `camcraft-*` edge is added. Decision record: `docs/decisions/163-tracing-libs.md`.

The issue's "Done means" is now covered across the three PRs: post writes name the file and result or why not (#222), a generation budget names its limit (#969, `a_budget_refusal_names_the_limit_that_fired_at_warn`), levels come from `CAMCRAFT_LOG`/`RUST_LOG` with a quiet `info` default (#222), and the library/UI prints that bypassed the filter are gone (this PR). No event was added inside a hot loop (the geometry profile lines stay behind their env var).

## How tested

- New pinning tests:
  - `camcraft-cl` `tests/refusal_log.rs::a_refused_axis_or_angle_is_a_warning_under_the_cl_target` - a refused move axis, C angle and builder axis are each a `WARN` event under `camcraft_cl`, and a stricter filter silences them.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`; Cargo changes fall back to batch scope): green on every test step in 27.9 min (geometry, kernel, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, ui suites all ok). The clippy step fails only on the pre-existing `MIN_LABEL_PX is never used` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/painted.rs:115` (upstream main, #2104, not touched here); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings -A dead_code` is clean.

title: feat(tools): convert STEP bodies to DXF half-profiles and import/export DXF
body:
## What changed

- Added a clean-room ASCII DXF writer in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/writer.rs` (`dxf::write`, `dxf::write_bytes`, `Unit::code`) emitting `HEADER` (`$INSUNITS`), `TABLES` (`LAYER`), and `ENTITIES` (`LINE`, `ARC`, `CIRCLE`).
- Added conservative stepped-band reduction in `crates/tools/src/spun_envelope.rs` (`SpunProfile::conservative_from_bands`) merging adjacent `HolderBand`s strictly upward (`max(r)`) down to at most 31 bands (`<= 64` points) and `MIN_SEGMENT`.
- Added STEP and `ToolBody` <-> ASCII DXF half-profile conversion and DXF import in `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf.rs` and `crates/app/src/tool_profile_dxf_import.rs` with explicit `CENTRELINE` and `PROFILE` layers.
- Added undoable `SetToolBody` constructors (`from_dxf_bytes`, `from_dxf`, `from_step_profile`, `from_placed_profile`, `profile_dxf`) in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body_dxf.rs` over `tool_body::build_spun`.
- Registered MCP tools `import_tool_holder_dxf`, `export_tool_holder_dxf`, and `convert_tool_step_to_profile` in `crates/app/src/mcp/holder_dxf_tools.rs`.
- Added conservative-envelope and half-profile-only notices, `Import DXF…`, `Export DXF…`, `Import STEP…`, and Body tab `Convert to profile` in `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs`, `tool_profile_page.rs`, and `tool_body_page.rs`.
- Recorded architectural trade-offs in `docs/decisions/743-step-dxf-half-profile.md`.

## Cause

- Direct conversion from `HolderProfile::envelope` to `SpunProfile` failed above 31 stepped bands because `2 * 32 + 2 = 66` exceeds `MAX_POINTS` (`64`).
- CamCraft lacked an ASCII DXF writer and could not export or re-import tool holder half-profiles with an explicit centreline or enforce ISO 13399 CSYS alignment on STEP-to-profile conversion.

## Tests

- Pins:
  - `camcraft-geometry::dxf_writer`: `write_and_parse_round_trip_lines_arcs_circles_layers_and_units`, `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name` (2 passed).
  - `camcraft-tools::spun::envelope::tests::thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile` (6 passed): `step_to_dxf_half_profile_envelops_every_sampled_mesh_point`, `non_revolved_step_or_fine_32_plus_band_mesh_is_conservatively_enveloped`, `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`, `dxf_half_profile_import_with_lines_and_arcs_lands_as_tool_body`, `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`, `round_trip_step_to_dxf_to_body_to_dxf_is_stable_within_tolerance`.
  - `camcraft-app::tool_dxf_profile_mcp`: `mcp_holder_dxf_and_step_profile_tools_list_round_trip_undo_and_refuse` (1 passed).
  - `camcraft-ui::egui_app::tests::tool_profile` (9 passed, adding `profile_tab_states_conservative_envelope_and_half_profile_rules_and_dxf_workflow` and `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`).
- Mutations (each tested red after weakening the guard and green after restore):
  - `spun_envelope::join` `max(r)` -> `min(r)`: failed `thirty_two_distinct_bands_reduce_conservatively_to_spun_profile`; restored green.
  - `dxf::writer` zero-length `LINE` guard bypassed: failed `writer_refuses_invalid_inputs_by_name`; restored green.
  - `tool_profile_dxf_import` centreline-crossing guard bypassed: failed `dxf_half_profile_error_refusals_never_panic_and_name_reasons`; restored green.
  - `step_to_spun_profile` ISO 13399 requirement replaced with `+Z` fallback: failed `step_conversion_refuses_missing_or_ambiguous_axis_by_name`; restored green.
  - `convert_body_draft_to_profile` clear-axis check bypassed: failed `body_tab_convert_to_profile_refuses_unaligned_step_and_converts_iso_aligned_step`; restored green.
- Gate:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` expanded to the `batch` tier (`crates/geometry/src/dxf/mod.rs` is a shared crate) and passed all 10 steps in 39.8 min with 0 failures (`geometry`, `kernel`, `cl`, `tools`, `post`, `sim`, `motion`, `app`, `ui`, `clippy -D warnings`).

## Goldens moved

- None (`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty).

## Not exercised

- Native OS file-picker modal calls (`import_profile_dxf_dialog`, `export_profile_dxf_dialog`, `import_step_profile_dialog`) delegate to desktop `rfd`; headless UI tests exercise `import_profile_dxf_from`, `export_profile_dxf_to`, `import_step_profile_from`, and `Convert to profile`.
- Release-tier `SLOW_BINARIES` (`motion:finish3d`, `motion:pivot5d`, `motion:flow`, `app:center_cut_multiaxis`) were outside the `batch` gate run.

- `#2092` (stacked on `#2054`) edits different functions in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs` (`library_body`, `SetToolBody::spun`), `crates/ui/src/state_tool_profile.rs` (`sync_tool_profile_ui`, `pick_library_holder`, `run_set_tool_holder`, `editor_library_holder`), `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_profile_page.rs` (lines 84-87), and `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` (lines 32, 38, 281); this PR uses `tool_body::build_spun` (no `ToolBody` struct literals) and companion modules/tail blocks; whichever merges second refreshes.

title: feat(motion): cut the adaptive stock ring from the air (issue 1950, rounds A-B)
body:
﻿Draft. Rounds A to E of issue #1950 (a default whole-model Adaptive 3D Pocket exceeds the planner budgets on the stock ring). This PR does not close the issue: the D plate level still goes to the Offset rings, now by the hop budget. Round F is open.

Head: c3509172c331eedacbf61f8a07855cadd12fdb75

## What changed

Round A (motion crate):
- New planner `plan_from_air` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs`. It cuts the stock ring from the air side inward. Sources: Held 1991 (LNCS 500), Held and Spielberger 2009 (CAD 41(7)), Stori and Wright 2000.
- `Raster::open_air` marks the air band as open. The walk functions of `raster.rs` moved to `raster/walk.rs` with no change of logic.

Round B (plumbing, no new algorithm):
- `machining3d::open_sides` takes a `stock_band` argument. `machining3d::stock_band(r, adaptive)` gives `2r + OPEN_SLACK` for Adaptive and `r - OPEN_SLACK` for each other strategy.
- New entry `machining3d::pocket3d_open_prev(facets, footprint, stock, p, mask)`. The stock goes through `ladder`, `hsm::plan_level`, `adaptive_passes` and `hsm_passes`.
- A plan from the air whose worst reading is over the load bound is refused by name. The level then goes to the Offset rings with a note.

Round C:
- App arm (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, `open_side.rs`): a whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy (not shell, not rest roughing) uses the wide band and calls `pocket3d_open_prev` with the setup stock outline. Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and each other strategy keep the old band.
- Microlift joins (`adaptive/air_links.rs`): each pass is joined to the one before it by the existing `LinkLaw`. Each join is walked again on the stock. A pass with no proved join keeps its retract hop. Source: Otkur and Lazoglu 2007.

Round D:
- Air entry: `machining2d::in_air(stock, e, r)`. Where the first pass of an air plan starts 0.005 mm clear of the stock outline, the ladder enters the level by an axial plunge there. A tool that is not centre-cutting keeps the old entry law.
- Fixture refusal: `air_band_refusal` refuses the Adaptive whole-model op at generation when a tagged fixture meets the air band. The message starts with `AIR_BAND_FIXTURE` and names the fixture. The post gate is not changed.

Round E:
- Cause of the round D crossing at (-8.12, -35.61). A probe printed the crossing pairs of the air passes before and after the joins. Before the joins: 40 pairs. After the joins: the same 40 pairs. So the joins and the air entry did not cause it. Pass 0 is the spiral (3 closed fronts and a closing lap on ring 3 at y -35.607). Passes 1-21 are open-front runs. Passes 22-45 are wall laps. The pairs were:
  - the spiral and the first open runs: a lead-in starts one load width back, on the ring 3 lap, and steps past it;
  - each open run and the run of the next front (1-4, 4-7, ...);
  - open runs and wall laps (4-37, 7-22, ...): a run that meets the part wall cuts across the laps.
- Fix, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_uncross.rs` (new): each new pass drops the chords that cross a kept pass, by the plan's own law (`guard::crosses`). The pass then continues as a new piece. Each piece is read on the stock as before, so the rest and the load readings stay true. Result: 0 crossing pairs before the joins.
- The joins: with the bare passes clean, `LinkLaw::late` (a lead whose graze joins the pass) put crossings back, because the lead runs back across an earlier pass. `air_joins` now keeps a late join only when the grown pass crosses no other pass. If it crosses, the join falls back to the retract hop. Result: 0 crossing pairs after the joins.
- The crossing check, the load check, the verify gate and the budgets are not changed.
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/descent.rs` (427 lines) is split. The landing spots (wall margin, spots along the first pass, the helix placement, the plunge spot) move to `machining3d/descent_place.rs` (120 lines) with no change of logic. `descent.rs` is now 327 lines.

## Readings, round E (D plate, R = 5, 70 x 70 stock, one level, debug)

| Reading | Round C/D (crossing plan) | Round E |
|---|---|---|
| Crossing through `adaptive_passes` | at (-8.12, -35.61) | none |
| Passes | 47 | 61 |
| Retract hops (budget 8) | 3 | 23 |
| Worst load (of D) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) | 0.153760 at (29.77, 22.31) |
| Slack to the bound | 0.00135 deg | 0.00135 deg |
| Moves (budget 120000) | 17614 | 17549 |
| Cut / air / lift (mm) | - / - / 107.3 | 2632 / 338 / 108 |
| Rest (limit 0.02) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| Time, one level (debug) | 21.8 s | 22.0 s |
| Strategy of the level | Offset rings (crossing) | Offset rings (hop budget) |

22 of the 23 hops are late joins that were refused because their lead crosses an earlier pass. The earlier reading of 3 hops came from joins whose leads crossed. The hop budget was not raised.

## Posted G-code

- Changed. Each whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy and a stock outline uses the wide band. A level whose air plan is clean and in its budgets is cut from the air. Other levels go to the Offset rings by name, as before.
- On the D plate, the stock ring level is still cut by the Offset rings (by name, now for the hop budget).
- Multi-Axis Rough, shell, rest roughing and the non-Adaptive strategies post as before.

## Pinning tests

- `machining2d::adaptive::air_uncross::tests::a_crossing_chord_is_dropped_and_the_pass_goes_on` (new).
- `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`: still red, now on the hop budget (23 over 8). Ignored with a round F reason.
- `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`: red on its hop assert (23 over 8). Ignored with a round F reason. Its rest and move asserts hold.
- `no_stock_keeps_the_growth_spiral`, `an_air_plan_over_the_load_bound_is_refused_by_name`: pass.
- `pocket3d_air_band`: 4 pass.

Round E runs:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib -- ring_tests air_rings air_uncross machining3d pocket adaptive`: 87 pass, 0 fail, 9 ignored (built before the descent split; the split is a move only, and clippy built it clean).
- App: `level_links` 25, `open_band` 7, `operations` 120 / 6 ignored, `pocket3d_air_band` 4, `pocket3d_hsm` 1 / 2 ignored, `pocket3d_open_side` 7, `whole_model_pocket` 5 / 1 ignored. All pass (after the split).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The heavy pin `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level` (`pocket3d_hsm`) was not run: the round E pin is not green.
- The motion lib filter did not run again after the descent split.
- `adaptive_pinch`, `area_controls`, `keep_law`, `narrow_band` and `neighbour_law` were not run in round E.
- No golden file changed. The heavy-lane move counts in `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs` and `stock_engine_agreement` can change at the cut.

## Open maintainer decisions (do not block)

- A load margin under the optimal load (worst load 0.153760, slack 0.00135 deg).
- The band for Multi-Axis Rough.

Changelog: Adaptive 3D Pocket: the stock ring around a whole model is cut from the air outside the stock where the plan is clean and in its budgets; the tool goes up to 2 tool radii past the stock side, and the passes are joined by microlifts. The level is entered by a plunge in the air outside the stock where that is proved clear. A tagged fixture in that band refuses the operation by name.

title: fix(post): Tormach lathe G76 J makes LinuxCNC's R1 ladder cut the record's passes
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`, `g76Grid`: J (first depth) is no longer floored to the grid on its own. LinuxCNC's G76 with `R1` cuts J, 2J, ... with the last pass clamped at K, so the control cuts ceil(K/J) passes. The record lays n = ceil(height / first depth) equal rungs (g76Why already holds the equal ladder), so J must satisfy (n-1)J < K <= nJ:

- J is the shallower grid rounding (as before) when that keeps the count;
- when the shallower J would add a pass, J is the one grid step up, and never a full grid step over the record's first cut;
- otherwise the record is refused by name: `G76 threading cycle refused - no first depth J on the control's grid makes R1's equal ladder cut the record's n passes (K ...)`.

The root keeps its outward rounding. Peak, root, I and K are unchanged.

## Golden change, line by line

`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc`, one line:

```
-G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0314 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
+G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0315 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0
```

What this relies on, from the public LinuxCNC G-code reference (G76): J is the first cut depth, K the full thread depth (diameters here, under G7), and `R1.0` selects constant depth, so each pass goes J deeper than the last and the last pass is clamped at K.
- Old: 0.0314, 0.0628, 0.0942, then 0.0944 (a 0.0002 in pass) = 4 passes. The record laid and the verdict judged 3 (0.4 / 0.8 / 1.2 mm radius).
- New: 0.0315, 0.0630, 0.0944 (clamped) = 3 passes, the record's count. J 0.0315 in is 0.000004 in (0.1 um) over the record's Ø0.8 mm first cut. The root (X + I - K) is the same as before: never deeper than the minor.
- P, Z, I, K, R, Q, H and every other line are unchanged. The mm golden (`J0.8 K2.4`) is byte-identical.

The earlier PathPilot Hub 8L sim run of this golden (PR #517 comments) does not cover the new J: **this golden needs a new Hub run** (not done here, no Hub access).

Scan (local script, not committed): realistic records (first depth 0.05-0.5 mm, height 0.3-2 mm, four minor diameters, the stream's lattice) - the old rule mis-stated 2.7% of inch records; the new rule miscounts none and refuses none in either unit. Refusals are reached only by records with many tiny rungs (e.g. 0.15 deep in rungs of 0.012, inch) or a lattice disagreement on the crest.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder.rs`:
- `g76_words_cut_exactly_the_records_passes_in_mm_and_inch` - parses the posted J/K as grid steps, counts ceil(K/J) and asserts it equals both the G33 pass count of the same document and ceil(height / first depth) of its record; asserts J is under one grid step over the record's first cut.
- `g76_refuses_by_name_when_no_grid_j_cuts_the_records_passes` - mm: crest +2 um (inside the lattice allowance) makes K 2.402, refused (J 0.801 would be a full step heavy); inch: 0.15 deep in 0.012 rungs, K 118 steps, no whole J with 12J < 118 <= 13J, refused.

Updated: `a_thread_posts_as_one_g76_block_with_the_option_in_mm_and_inch` (inch line J0.0315, golden regenerated).

Mutation checks (each mutation applied, suites run, file restored and touched):
- delete `if (j < lo) j = lo;` -> both new tests red (and the golden test);
- delete the refusal `return { why: ... }` line -> refusal test red;
- drop the `j <= hi` half of the refusal condition -> refusal test red (inch case);
- drop the `j - jRec < 1` half -> refusal test red (mm case).

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (post suites 5 s, app suites 1648 s - the shared golden pulled every app suite). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test lathe_post_tormach_g76_ladder --test lathe_post_tormach_thread -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised: a PathPilot / LinuxCNC run of the new inch golden; no batch gate (budget).

## Overlaps

- #517 and #518 (G76 on both lathe posts): `git merge-tree` with each branch is clean (#517 changes `g76Why`, this changes `g76Grid`), so not stacked. With #517's finish-allowance rule the record's rung count is still ceil(height / first depth).
- #1667 and #1681 conflict with this on adjacent lines of the same inch golden and `lathe_post_tormach_thread.rs` (their G30 / drive-line changes next to the G76 line): a mechanical keep-both, regenerate the golden at merge.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1619-g76-inch-ladder.md`.

Fork synced at v0.19.0 (branched from upstream/main 058e14ca).

Changelog: Tormach lathe G76 (inch) states a first depth J whose LinuxCNC R1 ladder cuts exactly the verified passes (J0.0315, not 0.0314, on the M12x2 fixture); a record no grid J can state is refused by name.

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(ui): keep a Geometry row's remove button in reach at the default window size
body: At the window's default size, a Geometry-tab selection row no longer runs past the Properties panel's edge: each row's × (remove this pick) is always on screen, and a label too long for the panel is shortened, with the whole label shown on hover. ## What changed `crates/ui/src/egui_app/geo_page.rs`, `chips`: a row was laid out as [Set origin buttons] [label] [×]. A face row's two Set origin buttons made it wider than the panel at 1280 × 800, so its label was cut off and its × was out of reach. Now: - the × comes first in the row, so it is always on screen; - the label takes the width that is left and is shortened with "…" when it doesn't fit (`egui::Label::truncate`, which shows the whole label on hover). The row hover from #1520 is unchanged: the label, the ×, the Set origin buttons and the row's own rectangle all still light the pick in the viewport. ## How tested - New: `egui_app::tests::geo_row_hover::every_rows_remove_button_is_in_reach_at_the_default_window_size`. At 1280 × 800 (`shell_window`'s default size), with a face, a chain and a vertex picked, every row's × is on screen, hovering it lights its pick, and clicking the face row's × removes the face pick. Without this change it fails: the face row's × sits at x = 1406. - The two existing `geo_row_hover` tests still pass, at their wide 2400 × 1000 window. - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (the `camcraft-ui` lib tests and the `boundary`, `boundary_picks`, `sinker_setup` and `theme_files` suites). - By hand in the desktop app on macOS, at the default window size, with the same three picks as the #1507 check (before / after screenshots below). **Before** (main, 1280 × 800): the face row's label is cut off and its × is past the panel edge. **After:** every row's × is on the left and in reach; long labels end in "…". **After:** hovering the face row's × lights its face. ## Not exercised - Windows and Linux by hand. The layout is plain egui, with nothing per platform. - Very narrow panels: the × and the Set origin buttons stay in reach down to about the width of the buttons themselves, below which egui clips them as before. Fork synced at v0.19.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 65); this branch merges `upstream/main` because the row hover from #1520 landed after v0.19.0. Changelog: Geometry tab: a selection row's remove button stays in reach at the default window size, and a long label is shortened with the full text on hover. title: fix(ui): disable unsupported browser menu file commands
body:
What changed
Theme Browse and the Fixtures menu file rows are disabled in the browser when unsupported. Their hover text gives the refusal reason. Desktop rows stay available. This completes the menu-state work left after merged PR #1438 added Save, Save As and Post downloads and merged PR #1314 added model and project pickers.

Fork synced at v0.19.0. This issue branch includes upstream/main through 4f4edcf.

Cause
Command dispatch refused these actions, but the menus still presented live rows. The menus now use the same refusal table and expose their disabled state to accessibility tools.

Tests
Pins: browser_theme_browse_is_disabled_with_a_reason and browser_fixture_file_rows_are_disabled_with_reasons. They check browser and desktop states, refusal text, and disabled clicks. The earlier run recorded both pins red before the fix. The earlier run also recorded restoration mutations: restoring each original menu file made its pin fail; restoring the fix made it pass. Fresh verification at 69a9825 passed both pins, cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main (4f4edcf; 1 step, 0 failures), and cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings. RUSTC_WRAPPER= avoided the previously recorded sccache infrastructure failure.

Goldens moved
None.

Not exercised
No browser session or wasm compilation was run for this fix.

Overlaps
Open PR #1639 also touches structural.rs, in different functions. These pins live in a separate child module.

Changelog: Unsupported browser Theme and Fixtures menu file commands are disabled with a reason (#1431).

Fixes #1431


## Screenshots

Rendered off-screen with the UI test harness in browser mode, using the default dark theme at 1280×720. BEFORE uses upstream/main (d2350d6a); AFTER uses PR head b706db9c. Upstream/main also has newer ribbon and browser styling; those surrounding differences are outside this PR.
